newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bank says post-IBM computer deal cheaper.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bank says post-IBM computer deal cheaper.

text.p: Argentina's state-run Banco Nacion said it can get a new computer system for $90 million, the bank's head said in a newspaper interview published Sunday.
Banco Nacion cancelled a $250 million deal with U.S. computer giant IBM last year amid a major bribery scandal.
"The new system will cost some $90 million, all included," Banco Nacion chairman Roque Maccarone told the Buenos Aires daily Clarin in an interview published Sunday.

Two separate reports -- one by the state auditing office and another conducted by a university at the request of a federal judge -- have concluded that the 1993 deal with International Business Machines Corp's local unit was wildly overpriced.
Banco Nacin sources told Clarn that unlike the cancelled IBM contract, the bank is now proceeding with a piecemeal, decentralized system of tenders.

Six international firms are vying for the main computer at Nacin headquarters, expected to cost some $10 million. Three others are competing for a $20 million contract to connect the headquarters system with computers at the bank's branches.
Those two are the largest contracts underway so far.
IBM, which is involved in a crossfire of lawsuits with Nacin, is not participating in the tenders.
Federal Judge Adolfo Bagnasco is investigating whether bribes were paid in 1993 to ensure that IBM clinched the deal.
Eleven people, including former Banco Nacin head Aldo Dadone and IBM Argentina's ex-President Ricardo Martorana and former Vice-President Gustavo Soriani, have been indicted in the case.
IBM Argentina has so far denied any wrongdoing, though it has admitted to errors and actions "inconsistent with company policy."
Banco Nacin last year cancelled the deal and sued IBM Argentina for $174 million, accusing it in a Buenos Aires commercial disputes court of not complying with deadlines.
IBM countersued for $86 million, alleging "wrongful revocation" of the contract.
Other IBM Argentina deals are under separate probes.
A separate judge is probing alleged "serious irregularities" in another $425 million contract and the awarding by decree of a deal between the firm and the country's tax collection body.
Another is probing why a deal between the company and the province of Mendoza government was awarded by decree instead of by tender.
